Maya (devex): FYI I'm hitting a weird client-side burst when using the python SDK paginate() + asyncio.gather combo. Server returns 429s but the client keeps sending. anyone seen parity issues between py/js here?

Omar (sdk): which python version? we shipped a change last month around token-bucket behavior; there was a bug where the bucket refill happened on the wrong event loop tick.

Maya (devex): repro is on 0.7.2. Minimal snippet:

```py
sem = asyncio.Semaphore(10)
async def worker(i):
  async with sem:
    async for page in client.paginate("/v1/responses", params):
      await process(page)

await asyncio.gather(*[worker(i) for i in range(100)])
```

Logs show 429s with Retry-After, but we still observe steady outgoing request rate and a bunch of subsequent 429s.

Omar (sdk): ugh. that matches the bug. paginate() yields control differently than single-request APIs, and our concurrency limiter wasn't being consulted on page fetches.

Sam (platform): server side we emit: `x-rate-limit-limit`, `x-rate-limit-remaining`, `x-rate-limit-reset` and honor `Retry-After`. If client parses Retry-After it should back off. Does the python SDK parse those headers on paginate endpoints?

Jules (eng-runtime): We also return a helpful 429 JSON payload with `suggested_backoff_ms`. But clients should fallback to Retry-After. If paginate callers do parallel page pulls, they can accidentally bypass per-route quotas.

Omar (sdk): confirming: python 0.7.2 missing header handling inside the paginator loop. We'll patch to parse Retry-After plus our `suggested_backoff_ms`. Quick workaround: set max_concurrency=1 on the client or wrap paginate with your own limiter and exponential jitter. Example workaround: 

```py
from backoff import expo, on_exception
@on_exception(expo, Exception, max_tries=8)
async def safe_fetch(page_fn):
    return await page_fn()

async for page in safe_paginate(client, ...):
    ...
```

Maya (devex): ok I'll try max_concurrency=1 and add a Retry-After handler in our sample app. can you add a unit test so this doesn't regress?

Omar (sdk): yup, adding test now. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/432 (draft). Will target a 0.7.3 hotfix tomorrow.

Maya (devex): thanks! I'll attach my repro logs and a tiny sample to the GH issue. also want to update onboarding sample app to show pagination + backpressure best-practices.

Jules (eng-runtime): long term we should emit a `x-client-retry-suggest` when we detect cascade 429s so SDKs can be smarter. filing infra idea.

Sam (platform): please coordinate with go-sdk owners too — parity matters. the go SDK currently has a semaphore that covers paginate but has slightly different jitter; we should standardize.

Omar (sdk): noted. will open parity checklist.

ci-bot: CI: test/rate-limiter flaked on feature/backpressure-fix — re-running. https://ci.redwood.ai/12345

Maya (devex): :thumbsup: will add a tiny e2e test to the sample app repo to catch this in future.

Omar (sdk): if anyone can DM me a minimal repro (even a recorded log snippet) I'll include it in the integration test harness.

Maya (devex): sending now. thanks all.
